name: Dispatch Guard
description: Middleware that enforces an orchestrator agent's output routing at the tool seam: denies deliverable-shaped writes (deliverable dirs/extensions, outside the whitelist) with a dispatch hint, warns on shell commands producing deliverables, and backstops a disabled spawn_subagent. Reads and basic file operations are never intercepted.

description_i18n.zh-CN: 在工具接缝层强制编排 agent 的产出路由：交付物形状的写入（交付物目录/扩展名，白名单外）直接拒绝并提示派发给对应 agent，shell 交付物启发式仅警告，spawn_subagent 兜底拦截。读操作与基础文件读写永不拦截。
description_i18n.en-US: Enforces an orchestrator agent's output routing at the tool seam: deny deliverable-shaped writes outside the whitelist, warn-only shell heuristics, spawn backstop. Reads and basic file operations are never intercepted.

author: CallMeHFK

meta.notes: No agent-facing tools. The plugin ships routes.example.json (a sanitized sample table); you write your own routes.json: in the plugin directory (explicit override, checked first) or in <host>/plugin-data/dispatch-guard/ (durable home that survives plugin reinstalls — the installer rebuilds the plugin directory on every install; the plugin mirrors the plugin-dir copy there after every reload). mode (enforce|warn|off, hot-reloaded by mtime in every mode — off keeps the middleware attached, passes calls unexamined, and records one action=off marker per disarmed period; a write to the guard's own table is the one thing off still refuses), deliverable_dirs / deliverable_exts (what counts as a deliverable — they extend the built-in defaults; non-string members are dropped with a warning), shell_enforce (opt-in deny of shell commands producing deliverables), write_tools (extra write-capable tool names; paths inside their arguments are scanned at any depth — data bodies such as content/text are prose, not paths), routes (keyword -> agent), ext_routes (extension -> agent). Two coverage tiers: explicit write targets — redirect (> >> >|), tee (short or long options), curl/wget -o/-O with the value separated or joined, dd of=, zip/tar create (short bundle or --create with --file/-f), compiler -o, sed/perl -i, --outdir/--output, cp/mv destination, ffmpeg positional output — follow the full write rules and can be denied; quoted mentions only warn. A broken routes.json no longer disarms the guard: parsing failure falls back to the last known-good table, only a cold cache with nothing good fails open to off. Tables are linted and type-normalized at load (contradictions, dead rules, unknown modes; a wrong-typed field, including a null/non-array match or a malformed manifest skills, degrades to absent instead of crashing). Only deliverable-shaped, non-whitelisted writes whose owner actually exists here are guarded: specialist agents are discovered from agents/*/agent.json manifests, a route naming an absent agent — or a readable inventory with zero agents — passes with a no_owner audit record (no owner, no block); the operator's table is trusted verbatim only when discovery could not read the layout — the walk failed, or a manifest exists but could not be opened. A fresh install drafts routes.draft.json (mode=warn, in the plugin-data dir, adopted not regenerated) from the discovered agents' declared dispatch policy — review it and rename to routes.json to activate; routes.json and routes.draft.json are private, gitignored, never packaged, and the guarded agent may not write them in any mode (meta-integrity) — by a write tool in any path shape or spelling, or via a shell command that mutates one of the two real table paths (absolute, resolved, or ~-spelled, boundary-anchored and case-insensitive; a bare basename after a cd into a guard home counts as well) — a command that only names one warns, and a project's own routes.json is never matched. Reads and basic writes (notes, scripts, configs, scratch) pass untouched in every mode; whitelist and deliverable matching are case-insensitive (Notes/ = notes/). Free-form task text is logged only as a digest (sha256+length+an excerpt filtered for known credential shapes such as sk- keys, AWS access key ids, Bearer headers and key=value assignments) — the same for a tool call whose shape the guard cannot parse. The filter is not a secret scanner, so an unrecognised credential can still appear in the capped excerpt; the hash, not the text, is the record's identity. Interception log: <workspace>/logs/dispatch_guard.jsonl (summarize with packaging/audit_summary.py). Design grounding: docs/RESEARCH.md
